summary: A short historical note from a Wikipedia-derived article on the United States' role in the Vietnam War, covering the start of formal U.S. military involvement in Indochina in May 1950. It reports that President Truman approved $10 million in military assistance after the Chinese People's Liberation Army captured Hainan Island from Chinese Nationalist forces. It also notes the establishment of a Defense Attaché Office in Saigon, which marked the beginning of formal U.S. military personnel assignments in Viet Nam.
one_line: In May 1950 Truman approved $10 million in aid for Indochina and the U.S. opened a Defense Attaché Office in Saigon, starting formal military presence in Vietnam.
key_facts: On May 1, 1950, President Truman approved $10 million in military assistance for anti-communist efforts in Indochina.
The approval came after the Chinese People's Liberation Army captured Hainan Island from Chinese Nationalist forces.
The Defense Attaché Office was established in Saigon in May 1950.
The establishment of the Defense Attaché Office was a formal recognition of Viet Nam (vice French IndoChina).
The Defense Attaché Office marked the beginning of formal U.S. military personnel assignments in Viet Nam.
U.S. Naval, Army and Air Force personnel established their respective attaches at this time.
The Defense Attaché Office was set up in Saigon, the capital of Viet Nam at the time.
The May 1950 steps are recorded as the beginning of formal U.S. military involvement in Viet Nam.
